title: Fair usage cap prototype — personal notebook
content:
Goal: sketch a lightweight, PLG-friendly fair-usage cap system that prevents cost abuse (spikes, scraping) but doesn't block legitimate rapid experimentation. Keep as simple as possible for initial rollout; we can evolve to predictive smoothing later.

Top-level constraints / goals
- free/low-tier must be forgiving for early dev iteration (fast feedback loop)
- avoid abrupt hard blocks that hurt activation and virality
- measurable unit economics: tie cap constructs to clear cost backfills (GPU time / token cost)
- implementable with existing quota + rate-limit infra (we have per-key quotas + token meters + simple throttles)

Key primitives to play with
- soft cap (daily rolling token budget) + burst bucket that refills slowly
- overage mode: graceful degradation (reduce generation length, route to cheaper model, increase sampling temperature?) — prefer cheaper model fallback for throughput vs quality tradeoff
- token burn accounting: charge generation+prompt tokens separately; track per-request breakdown so we can surface it in Console
- fairness window: 24h rolling + weekly smoothing to let binge usage smooth out a bit

Assumptions (ballpark numbers for back-of-envelope)
- infra token marginal cost (hosted): $0.00018 per 1k tokens served on average mix (blended across models and batching) — derived from fleet avg GPU hr amortized / token output; see crude cost sheet.
- avg dev request: 400 prompt tokens, 1500 generation tokens (1.9k total) — interactive assistants, prototype usage
- conv embedding lookups (search) add 512 tokens per use on average for context generation flows
- free-tier allowance target: let a user run ~25-50 full interactive sessions before hitting soft cap; want to avoid gating during onboarding

Quick math: tokens -> infra cost per session
- per-session tokens (prompt+generate) = 1.9k tokens -> 1.9 * $0.00018 per 1k = $0.000342 (i.e. ~0.034 cents) — this number feels low vs reality but remember blended cost; conservatively multiply by 3 for overhead = $0.00102 (~0.1 cents).
- if a new user does 50 sessions in onboarding -> cost ~= $0.051 per user. Good for PLG free credits.

Soft-cap design options (tradeoffs)
1) Daily rolling token budget + unblock path
   - free: 500k tokens/day soft cap (refill continuously). Bursts allowed up to 2x for first hour.
   - micro payg: 2M tokens/day per-key soft cap, then throttle to 5 requests/min until next window.
   - rationale: simple to implement with existing per-key token counters and rate-limiting.
   - pros: predictable, easy to explain. Cons: non-intuitive for users who do heavy batch work.

2) Credit-bucket with reserve and micro-billing
   - each account gets a small rolling credit balance; when credits depleted, we start micro-billing per-1k tokens at PAYG rate with no hard block.
   - better for converting power users immediately.
   - downside: requires billing plumbing for tiny charges; complexity.

3) Hybrid: soft cap + cheaper fallback model + optional opt-in payg overflow
   - on soft cap breach: route generation to a quantized/cheaper variant (lower perf). Offer popup: "switch to PAYG overflow to keep using premium model".
   - low cognitive load, nudges conversion.

Fairness rules (edge cases)
- batch jobs / single long runs: allow explicit 'batch' flag so system treats as non-interactive and applies different caps (higher daily tokens but strict per-minute throughput).
- embeddings-heavy apps: separate cap for embedding tokens vs completion tokens (embedding tokens cheaper infra-per-token but heavily used) — prevents embedding-only apps from consuming all free allowance and blocking text generation experimentation.
- multi-key customers (service accounts): cap at organization aggregate with per-key soft caps to avoid sharding abuse.

Simplified policy prototype (very rough)
- Free dev account:
  * 1M tokens rolling 24h soft cap
  * burst allowance: up to 2.5M within any 1h window if account is new (<30d)
  * on soft cap: fallback to cheap-model route (quantized small model) for up to additional 1M tokens; warn client via response header and Console toast
  * optional: allow payg-overflow at $0.0006 / 1k tokens (premium model price) TTL until org adds billing method
- PAYG account:
  * 10M tokens rolling 24h soft cap, on exceed -> rate-limited to 10 req/s or route to cheapest compatible variant
  * immediate billing for overage at standard PAYG rate
- Enterprise / committed: configurable per-contract (no automatic hard caps, but alerting + surge protection)

Back-of-envelope revenue conversion thought
- If 1k trial signups -> 20% convert to paid within 30d; avg paid customer first-month consumption ~ 5M tokens -> revenue (PAYG blended price $0.002 / 1k) = 5M/1k * $0.002 = $10/mo per converted user; CAC and churn aside, seems plausible for small teams.
- but committed customers drive most ARR; the cap system should be conservative enough to steer high-usage accounts to commit.

UX notes / product copy thoughts
- Show "estimated infra cost" for current usage in Console (e.g., "You're burn ~ $0.05 today") — transparency helps convert and reduces billing disputes.
- When routing to cheap-model fallback, include header: X-Redwood-Fallback: cheap-model-v1 and a short reason code for observability.
- Provide a developer toggle: "allow payg overflow" for free accounts (default off) to avoid surprise charges during onboarding.

Implementation checklist (minimal viable)
- [ ] per-key rolling 24h token counters (exists) + implement burst window calculation
- [ ] cheap-model routing config per account + response header tagging
- [ ] Console: soft-cap banner + usage estimate + payg overflow opt-in flow
- [ ] Billing: support micro-overflow charges or simple conversion flow to full PAYG billing
- [ ] Metrics: track soft-cap breaches, fallback rates, conversion rate post-breach

Open questions / TODOs
- What is the true blended infra marginal cost per 1k tokens? Current $0.00018 is very rough; need infra team microbenchmark across our model catalog with realistic seq distributions (ping SRE/infra).
- How do we prevent cost gaming where users rotate keys to reset soft caps? Need org-level rollups and heuristics (IP fingerprinting?).
- Legal / refund policy for accidental payg overflow charges — product + finance to define.
- Will fallback routing/regenerate semantics confuse users building quality-sensitive flows (e.g., summarization)? Possibly need route-by-intent override.

Notes to self:
- Chat with @Jonas about threshold heuristics (he's got usage histograms for last 6 months).
- Draft a simple explainer diagram for Console team (flow: normal -> soft cap -> fallback -> payg prompt).
- Run cohort sim: pick 10k anonymous trial accounts, simulate using our daily histograms and see % that would hit soft cap under different thresholds.

End of notebook — keep this lightweight. If leads like approach, formalize in PRIC-134 doc and propose for Q2 rollout.
